concepts.learning_objective: Describe the properties of cathode rays and how they established the electron.
Use Thomson's e/m ratio and Millikan's charge to obtain the mass of the electron.
Recall how protons and neutrons were discovered and their properties.

topics.title: Atomic Models, Atomic Number and Isotopes

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the Thomson and Rutherford models and interpret the alpha-scattering results.
Calculate protons, neutrons and electrons from atomic number and mass number.

topics.title: Wave and Particle Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation

concepts.learning_objective: Relate frequency, wavelength and wavenumber of electromagnetic radiation.
Apply Planck's quantum theory to the photoelectric effect.
State Bohr's postulates, including quantised angular momentum and energy.
Calculate energies and wavelengths of transitions in the hydrogen atom.
Identify the limitations of Bohr's model.

topics.title: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model: Dual Behaviour and Uncertainty

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the de Broglie relation to microscopic and macroscopic particles.
Explain Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and its consequences.

topics.title: Orbitals, Quantum Numbers and Shapes of Orbitals

concepts.learning_objective: Assign allowed values of n, l, ml and ms to electrons in orbitals.
Determine the number of radial and angular nodes of orbitals.

topics.title: Energies of Orbitals and Electronic Configuration

concepts.learning_objective: Order orbital energies using the (n + l) rule and the aufbau principle.
State and apply the Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule.
Explain the extra stability of half-filled and completely filled subshells.
